title: Insecure output handling: shell command injection through file_stats
summary: The lab classes this as command injection (ASI05). In the lab as built, the effect is a simulated list of spawned commands.

LC.rationale: The finding states the filename argument is attacker-influenced through injection or the user, and the lab's data sources include attacker-controllable fetched web pages, so attacker-controlled language enters through ingested content and reaches the file_stats tool-invocation path.

CP.rationale: The baseline memory is a cross-session JSON file of free-text notes that the next session's system prompt presents as trusted instructions, and the remember tool saves free text even after untrusted content was read.

AP.rationale: The lab is a single agent with no handoffs and multi-agent setups out of scope, so the effect is confined to the initially affected component.

RH.rationale: The file_stats sink is a shell simulator that only lists commands and executes nothing, and the PoC is a direct tool call asserting on simulated commands, so no verified reward-hacking episode exists though the simulated command path is reachable.

ES.rationale: The baseline offers all twelve built-in tools with unvalidated arguments, and remote MCP tool descriptions and schemas are fetched every run and trusted unpinned and unscanned.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models the agent as a tool-using office assistant whose model chooses tool calls and arguments, with scripted worst-case models used in the exploit tests.
